newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urged to fight misuse of the Internet.
newsitem.headline: EU urged to fight misuse of the Internet.

text.p: European Union governments, industry groups and parents should unite to fight child pornography and other illegal or harmful material on the Internet, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

The EU executive, under pressure to act in the wake of a child-sex scandal in Belgium, issued two reports on ways to protect children and to prevent criminals such as terrorists from misusing the global computer network.

It shied away from proposing strict legislation, however, instead offering solutions such as industry codes of conduct, cooperation between the 15 EU governments to enforce existing laws and software that can screen out unwanted material.

Governments should consider, however, whether an EU legal framework was needed to clarify whether companies that offer access to the Internet should be responsible for its content, the Commission said.
It stressed that it was trying to find an approach that did not threaten freedom of expression.
"We are not proposing a measure that could be misconstrued as censorship," Industrial Affairs Commissioner Martin Bangemann told a news conference.

The Commission said industry codes of conduct should guarantee that all material on the Internet is traceable. It also highlighted a new technical standard known as PICS that allows information on the Internet to be labelled and filtered out.

EU industry ministers agreed last week that Germany should host an international conference of law enforcement authorities and industry representatives to discuss whether to draw up an international convention on illegal and harmful content on the Internet.
The question has been in the spotlight in recent months following the deaths of four girls in Belgium that were linked to a paedophile network.
Belgian Telecommunications Minister Elio di Rupo asked the EU to take action to keep material featuring sexual abuse or exploitation of children off the Internet.
EU telecoms ministers will discuss the question in November.
